caps.text:
6 things i learned reading sleep studies
(some of them annoyed me)

Night Shift didn't help

in a trial of 167 people aged 18–24, sleep was the same with Night Shift on or off. the filter isn't the fix

30 minutes changes a lot

students who slept badly put the phone down 30 min before bed: they fell asleep ~12 min faster and slept ~18 min longer

"bedtime procrastination" is a real research term

going to bed late when nothing is stopping you. nothing except the phone

6 in 10 people under 30 are on their phone in the last 10 minutes before sleep

and in the first 10 after waking

snoozing isn't the villain

in a lab study, 30 min of snoozing didn't make regular snoozers groggier or moodier

a regular schedule mattered

students who slept at the same times got better grades than ones who didn't, even with similar hours

so i built my app around the phone, not the alarm

my apps stay asleep in the morning until i've walked 200 steps
